correctness.rationale: The finite classification is correct. An independent enumeration of all binary relations with total side size below six found no two relation-isomorphism classes sharing an ordered dual-Dowker signature. For \(3\times3\), independent enumeration found 174 labeled bi-twin-free matrices, eight row/column-isomorphism classes, seven ordered dual-Dowker signatures, and signature multiplicities \(1,1,1,1,1,1,2\). The unique two-class fiber has canonical strings `001011111` and `011101111`, matching the displayed matrices. Their row-degree multisets differ, so they are not relation-isomorphic, while each side has a full 2-simplex as Dowker complex. The lower-size argument also follows directly from the distinct-nonempty-neighborhood constraint.
risks: The result is a minimal finite boundary only; no classification of larger fibers is proved.
sources: independent exhaustive reconstruction of every relevant matrix and signature

Neither inspected full text gives the stronger two-sided question after both row and column twins and empties are removed, nor the exact first-loss census. The complete \(3\times3\) minimal collision therefore survives as original to the best of the inspected evidence.
